provenance.reviewers: 4 read-only Sonnet subagents (correctness, security, ticket-fit, tests briefs)

findings.title: PUT without vetId clears the stored vet
findings.source: correctness, security, ticket-fit and tests reviewers
findings.observation: A client that omits vetId wipes the existing vet; "leave unchanged" cannot be told from "clear".
findings.why: PUT replaces the whole visit, so clearing persists, as ticket item 2 demands. See the assumption.

findings.title: Unknown vetId answers a bare 404, not a 400
findings.observation: A stale or bogus vetId fails the booking or edit with the generic "Not found!" 404, indistinguishable from a missing visit or pet.
findings.why: same as unknown pet types, OwnerRestController.java:150; a 400 belongs in a codebase-wide change.

findings.title: Vet ids can be enumerated via the 404
findings.observation: Probing vetIds on booking reveals which vets exist.
findings.why: GET /api/vets lists every vet already; nothing is disclosed.

findings.title: Visits expose vet names to every caller
findings.observation: Visit DTOs now carry the vet's first and last name.
findings.why: Visit endpoints are OWNER_ADMIN-only and vet names are already public via /api/vets.

findings.title: Any existing vet can be attributed to a visit
findings.observation: No check that the chosen vet may attend the visit.
findings.why: choosing any vet is the feature; the ticket sets no eligibility rule.

findings.title: Chatbot create_visit cannot choose a vet
findings.observation: Bookings made through the chatbot always have no vet.
findings.why: the vet is optional at booking; owners rarely know it. Separate ticket if wanted.

findings.title: Failed vets fetch shows "No vet" for a visit with one
findings.observation: The error handler turns a failed GET /vets into [], so the combo finds no match and displays the placeholder.
findings.why: model keeps the old vetId, so saving does not clear it; display-only, error path.

findings.title: Clearing the combo could send '' or 0
findings.observation: The edit spec feeds onSubmit a hand-built null; if the combo emitted '' or 0 on clear, the old vet or a 404 would follow.
findings.why: pick('') sets null, line 57; covered by the combo's own spec.

findings.title: Pipe renders "null null" with vetId but no names
findings.observation: A visit with vetId set but names missing would print "null null".
findings.why: VisitMapper.java:51-53 sets id and both names together from one entity.

autofixes.title: Vet tests read the session cache, not the database
autofixes.observation: VisitTest is @Transactional and only one test cleared the persistence context, so create/update/clear read back the cached entity. A broken vet_id mapping or a clear that never reached the row would still pass.
autofixes.fix: a flushAndClear() helper runs after every write the vet tests then assert on.

autofixes.title: Unknown vetId on edit and on owner-page booking untested
autofixes.observation: Only POST /api/visits had an unknown-vet test; PUT /api/visits/{id} and POST /owners/{o}/pets/{p}/visits could regress to a 500 unnoticed.

autofixes.title: Deleting a vet with visits is untested
autofixes.observation: Keeping a deleted vet's visits rests on ON DELETE SET NULL in V4, and nothing exercised it; the delete could fail on the foreign key.
autofixes.fix: test deletes a vet through the API and reads the visit back with no vet.

autofixes.title: Chatbot list_visits omits the vet
autofixes.observation: The ticket says visits show their vet everywhere, yet the MCP list_visits answer had no vet field.
autofixes.fix: VisitView carries vetName, null when the visit has none.

assumptions.title: PUT replaces the visit; a missing vetId means no vet
assumptions.alternative: PATCH-like: absent keeps the vet, explicit null clears it
assumptions.why: Ticket item 2 makes "clear must stick" the priority, and full-replace PUT is the simplest rule that guarantees it; the only client, our edit form, always sends the field. Four reviewers flagged the omitted-field case, which pulls confidence down.

assumptions.title: Unknown vetId is a 404
assumptions.alternative: 400 naming vetId as the bad field
assumptions.why: Matches how unknown pet types are handled. A 400 is more correct HTTP, which is why this is close to a coin flip.

assumptions.title: Deleting a vet keeps their visits, with no vet
assumptions.alternative: refuse deleting a vet who has visits
assumptions.why: Ticket item 4 makes "no vet" a normal state, and before this change vet deletion always succeeded. Losing who attended is a real history loss, so a business owner could reasonably pick refusal.

assumptions.title: "No vet" is the wording for a visit without one
assumptions.why: Ticket item 4 rules out "Unknown" and blank; "No vet" says "has none" literally, and the same label serves as the combo placeholder.

assumptions.title: Seed gives a vet to some demo visits only
assumptions.alternative: leave every seeded visit without a vet
assumptions.why: The demo should show both states; ticket item 4 is about real legacy rows, not the demo dataset.

assumptions.title: MCP create_visit takes no vet; list_visits shows it
assumptions.alternative: also add a vet parameter to create_visit
assumptions.why: "Everywhere" in the ticket covers displaying, which list_visits does; choosing a vet at booking stays a staff action in the UI.
